question: Which of the following is an example of objective nutritional documentation?

options.A: Patient hates hospital food because it tastes bland and boring
options.B: Patient reports eating fresh vegetables once a week and skipping breakfast
options.C: Patient is lazy and refuses to eat the nutritious food provided by the hospital
options.D: Patient has a terrible diet and clearly does not care about health

explanation: Objective documentation relies on factual, descriptive statements without personal opinions or judgmental language. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h7)

question: Why is getting support from religious and traditional leaders important for youth health programs?

options.A: It reduces community stigma and builds adult support for youth health initiatives
options.B: It eliminates the need for trained nurses in rural health posts
options.C: It makes health facilities exempt from paying local taxes
options.D: It gives leaders the authority to prescribe medications to teenagers

explanation: When community leaders understand and back the program, it eases resistance and helps parents feel good about their teens receiving care.

question: Where do isolation precautions mostly try to break the chain of infection?

options.A: At the mode of transmission
options.B: At the patient's genetic code
options.C: Inside the patient's bloodstream
options.D: Inside the pharmacy storage room

explanation: Barriers like masks, gloves, and private rooms primarily stop germs from traveling from one place to another. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h2)

question: What helpful role do the resident bacteria in your colon play?

options.A: Digesting the majority of dietary fats and proteins
options.B: Producing protective mucus for the rectal lining
options.C: Synthesizing certain vitamins and fermenting fiber
options.D: Preventing all water absorption to keep stool soft

explanation: Correct! Our gut bacteria are friendly helpers that break down fiber and even manufacture important nutrients like vitamin K for us.

question: Why are tiny air particles like PM2.5 so dangerous to our health?

options.A: They react with sunlight to form ozone gas
options.B: They bypass upper airway filters and reach deep lung tissues
options.C: They create a visible yellow haze over industrial cities
options.D: They dissolve completely in the saliva inside the mouth

explanation: Great job! Because they are so tiny, PM2.5 particles slip right past our nose and throat defenses and go straight into the tiny air sacs in our lungs.

question: What is the primary function of GABA in the central nervous system?

options.A: To trigger happy memories in the frontal lobe
options.B: To stimulate muscle movement in the arms and legs
options.C: To calm nervous system activity and reduce anxiety
options.D: To increase blood pressure during a physical threat

explanation: GABA is the main inhibitory neurotransmitter, meaning it slows down brain activity to keep anxiety levels manageable. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h3)

question: A confused elderly patient keeps holding pills in their cheek without swallowing them. What is this behavior called?

options.A: First-pass effect
options.B: Pouching
options.C: Aspiration
options.D: Enteric coating

explanation: Pouching happens when patients store food or medication in their cheek pockets instead of swallowing it. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h6)

question: A nurse is preparing a patient for an emergency cesarean section in a busy unit. What is the best way to use the safety checklist?

options.A: Pause and verify each safety step out loud with the surgical team
options.B: Ignore the checklist because the team is in a hurry to save time
options.C: Ask the patient to fill out the surgical checklist by herself
options.D: Sign the checklist at the end of the shift without checking the patient

explanation: Checklists are most effective when the healthcare team pauses to verify items collaboratively out loud before proceeding. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h5)

question: How does the stress-relaxation response help an organ like your urinary bladder?

options.A: It forces the organ to empty immediately when it reaches half capacity
options.B: It prevents the muscle cells from ever fatiguing during hard work
options.C: It generates rapid pumping movements to mix internal contents
options.D: It allows the organ to stretch to hold more fluid without a sharp pressure spike

explanation: This clever response lets your bladder gradually accommodate more fluid as it fills up, preventing sudden uncomfortable pressure spikes. Nursing clinicals will make this super clear too!

question: In a standard research dataset, what does each row typically represent?

options.A: A summary of missing values
options.B: The final statistical conclusion
options.C: A different measurement scale
options.D: A single participant or subject

explanation: Standard datasets are arranged so that each horizontal row corresponds to one individual participant, while the vertical columns represent the variables measured. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h1)

question: Up to what level should you fill a safety box before closing it for disposal?

options.A: Emptied out daily regardless of level
options.B: Sealed only when the outer cardboard tears
options.C: Never filled beyond the three-quarter line
options.D: Packed completely to the very top rim

explanation: You got it! Stopping at the three-quarter mark ensures protruding needles don't accidentally prick anyone passing by.

question: What is a common misconception about the health status of HIV orphans?

options.A: People assume all orphans are infected with HIV themselves
options.B: People assume orphans never require routine immunizations
options.C: People think orphans are immune to childhood malnutrition
options.D: People believe orphans cannot contract malaria or typhoid

explanation: Not every child who loses a parent to HIV has the virus. Many are negative and simply suffering from poverty and loss. Keep this distinction clear in your practice!

question: Which of the following is a major ethical concern when using electronic health records?

options.A: The physical weight of computer monitors on the ward
options.B: The cost of buying ink for hospital printers
options.C: The bright lighting of phone screens in dark rooms
options.D: Patient privacy and data security risks

explanation: Protecting confidential health information from unauthorized access or cyber threats is a primary ethical duty for all nurses. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of cinchonism in a patient taking quinine?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the sclera
options.B: Severe swelling of the tongue
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle twitching
options.D: Ringing in the ears (tinnitus)

explanation: You're doing great! Tinnitus (ringing in the ears), dizziness, and mild blurred vision are hallmark clues of quinine overdose (cinchonism).

question: What does publishing nursing research primarily help the profession establish?

options.A: Total control over all medical school curricula
options.B: A unique and independent body of knowledge
options.C: The right to practice medicine without a license
options.D: Exemption from hospital ethical oversight boards

explanation: Spot on! Having our own distinct set of scientific knowledge is what truly makes nursing a respected, independent profession.

question: What is the main health benefit of encouraging child spacing through family planning after having a baby?

options.A: It gives the mother's body time to recover its nutrient stores and strength.
options.B: It makes uterine involution happen within twenty-four hours.
options.C: It guarantees that the next baby will be a male child.
options.D: It completely stops all postpartum mood changes.

explanation: Pregnancy takes a lot out of a woman's body! Spacing pregnancies gives her time to rebuild her iron and nutrient levels so she stays strong for herself and her family.

question: What actually makes a dietary protein source 'complete'?

options.A: It comes exclusively from plant-based foods
options.B: It contains all nine essential amino acids
options.C: It is completely digested within one hour
options.D: It contains zero fats and zero carbohydrates

explanation: Essential amino acids are the ones our bodies can't manufacture on their own. A complete protein food gives us all nine of them in one go!

question: What are the three main pillars of health financing?

options.A: Raising, pooling, and purchasing
options.B: Planning, staffing, and evaluating
options.C: Insuring, billing, and auditing
options.D: Prescribing, dispensing, and storing

explanation: Think of health financing as collecting funds (raising), putting them together to share risks (pooling), and paying for care (purchasing). You've got this!

question: Why is it important for a nurse manager to stay flexible while running a program?

options.A: Staff members prefer working without a fixed schedule
options.B: Government rules require changing the budget every week
options.C: It stops patients from asking questions about their care
options.D: Unforeseen challenges like transport breakdowns often occur

explanation: That's true! Unexpected hurdles happen all the time in real life, so a good manager adapts quickly to keep things moving.

question: Which of the following best describes the multi-faceted role of a nurse working in a Nigerian primary health center?

options.A: Acting as a clinician, educator, manager, and community advocate
options.B: Writing laws and policies for the federal parliament
options.C: Performing complex heart surgeries in a private luxury suite
options.D: Working strictly as an accountant in a corporate bank office

explanation: PHC nurses handle diverse responsibilities, from treating patients and teaching families to managing clinic supplies and leading community health outreach. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h10)

question: Which nursing diagnosis fits best for a patient struggling with painful bladder spasms and trouble urinating due to an enlarged prostate?

options.A: Impaired urinary elimination
options.B: Risk for impaired skin integrity
options.C: Ineffective tissue perfusion
options.D: Excess fluid volume

explanation: An enlarged prostate blocks the normal flow of urine, directly leading to an alteration in urinary elimination. Perfect match for the nursing care plan!

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of a strong healthcare referral network?

options.A: Isolating the client from all family and friends
options.B: Ensuring continuity of medical follow-up
options.C: Providing access to professional social workers
options.D: Connecting the client with community support groups

explanation: Good referral networks are designed to build a strong safety net and reduce isolation, never to cut a client off from the people who love and support them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h7)

question: Which of these bones develops directly through intramembranous ossification?

options.A: Tibia of the lower leg
options.B: Humerus of the upper arm
options.C: Femur of the thigh
options.D: Flat bones of the skull

explanation: Great job! Flat bones (like your skull and jaw) form directly from sheets of tissue without needing a cartilage model first.

question: Why do adults in a holoendemic community often show no symptoms of the disease?

options.A: The local climate prevents the disease germ from surviving in adults
options.B: They caught the infection and built immunity during early childhood
options.C: Adult bodies naturally destroy the germ before it can enter the blood
options.D: Traditional herbal medicines protect adults from getting sick

explanation: In holoendemic settings, almost everyone gets infected very early in life, leaving surviving adults with strong long-term immunity. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h1)

question: What is the primary job of the Dorsal Respiratory Group in the medulla?

options.A: Triggering active exhalation during heavy exercise
options.B: Driving the basic automatic rhythm of inhalation
options.C: Controlling voluntary speech patterns during breathing
options.D: Detecting blood oxygen levels directly in the lungs

explanation: The dorsal respiratory group acts as the natural pacemaker for normal, quiet breathing so you don't have to think about every breath.

question: What is the primary purpose of nursing research?

options.A: To eliminate the need for patient preferences
options.B: To develop trustworthy evidence for nursing practice
options.C: To increase the cost of hospital operations
options.D: To replace clinical judgment with rigid rules

explanation: Nursing research systematically gathers facts to guide safe and effective care choices. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why do we often use a mix of different therapies to manage chronic pain in patients with physical disabilities?

options.A: Single medications are completely ineffective for all types of nerve pain
options.B: Non-pharmacological methods remove the need for any clinical supervision
options.C: Combining different therapies addresses multiple underlying causes of pain safely
options.D: Pain associated with physical disabilities always resolves spontaneously

explanation: Chronic pain has many layers, so combining meds and physical therapy gives better relief without needing dangerously high drug doses. Smart approach!

question: What is the most important first step when a nurse needs to assess a patient who has undergone FGM?

options.A: Building trust and providing a safe, private environment
options.B: Performing a physical exam before talking to the patient
options.C: Asking family members to step outside permanently
options.D: Notifying local law enforcement immediately

explanation: You've got it! Because FGM involves deep trauma and shame, you must always build trust and create a safe space before any exam or questioning.

question: Why does a patient often experience bad chills right before their temperature shoots up with a fever?

options.A: The kidneys are failing to filter out toxic waste products
options.B: The nervous system is reacting to a sudden drop in room temperature
options.C: Blood vessels are dilating to release trapped heat from the skin
options.D: The muscles are rapidly contracting to generate internal heat

explanation: Exactly! Shivering is just your muscles moving quickly to build up warmth so your body can reach its new, higher fever setting.

question: A patient has damage to their cochlea and auditory nerve. What type of hearing loss is this?

options.A: Sensorineural hearing loss
options.B: Central processing loss
options.C: Mixed hearing loss
options.D: Conductive hearing loss

explanation: When the inner ear structures (like the cochlea) or the hearing nerve itself are damaged, we call it sensorineural hearing loss.

question: If an expectant mother reports a sudden decrease in fetal movement, what should you suspect first?

options.A: The fetus has dropped into the pelvic cavity
options.B: The mother is simply too busy to notice kicks
options.C: Normal sleeping patterns of a full-term baby
options.D: Potential fetal distress or oxygen deprivation

explanation: Always take a drop in baby kicks seriously! It can be a vital warning sign that the baby is under distress and needs an urgent check-up.

question: What is the primary effect of patriarchal structures on family health responsibilities?

options.A: Men take on all nursing duties at home
options.B: Children become responsible for their own care
options.C: Health and domestic matters are left entirely to women
options.D: Couples share all medical decisions equally

explanation: Patriarchal norms often assign all caregiving and domestic duties to women, keeping men away from health spaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h2)

question: What usually happens when a hospital's stated values do not match how its leaders actually behave?

options.A: Trust dissolves rapidly among staff and stakeholders
options.B: The organization immediately goes bankrupt by law
options.C: State licensing boards automatically lower facility taxes
options.D: Employees begin working harder to compensate for leaders

explanation: When leaders say one thing and do another, hypocrisy kills workplace trust and staff morale very quickly.

question: Why is it smart to adjust alarm limits on a portable monitor for each specific patient?

options.A: The machine will refuse to record data without personalized input
options.B: Standard defaults are illegal to use in modern hospitals
options.C: Customizing limits stops the battery from draining too quickly
options.D: Factory defaults may be unsafe or cause unnecessary alarm fatigue

explanation: Generic settings can either miss a real problem or beep constantly for no reason (alarm fatigue). Tailoring it to the patient keeps everyone sane and safe!

question: During which phase of the PDSA cycle does the nursing team actually carry out the test and record initial observations?

options.A: Plan
options.B: Study
options.C: Act
options.D: Do

explanation: Awesome! The 'Do' phase is when you roll up your sleeves, try out the idea on a small scale, and write down what happens.

question: Why is activated charcoal often instilled right before the lavage tube is removed?

options.A: To lubricate the tube so it slips out of the throat without friction
options.B: To stimulate normal bowel movements and speed up total digestion
options.C: To neutralize any acidic cleaning fluids remaining in the stomach wall
options.D: To catch and bind any remaining toxin particles left behind in the gut

explanation: Charcoal binds tightly to residual toxins that escaped the physical washing process, preventing them from entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h6)

question: Which hygiene practice should nurses advise patients to avoid to protect their cervix?

options.A: Using scented vaginal douches and chemical sprays
options.B: Washing the external vulva with plain warm water
options.C: Wearing loose-fitting cotton undergarments daily
options.D: Changing sanitary pads frequently during menstruation

explanation: Correct! Douching and scented products mess with the vagina's natural balance and easily irritate delicate tissues.

question: Why is keeping a food diary helpful for someone with gas issues?

options.A: It completely cures lactose intolerance without any medication.
options.B: It measures the exact volume of gas produced each hour.
options.C: It helps the patient and nurse pinpoint specific foods that trigger excess gas.
options.D: It guarantees the patient will lose weight within the first week.

explanation: Writing down meals and symptoms helps connect the dots so patients can figure out which foods don't agree with them.

question: What usually happens when health professionals bypass community input and decide problems alone?

options.A: Government funding increases because the staff showed independence
options.B: The community completes all health projects much faster
options.C: They often target issues that do not match the real priorities of the residents
options.D: Local disease rates drop instantly due to professional expertise

explanation: Without local consultation, healthcare workers may focus on problems that matter to textbooks rather than the community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h5)

question: Who is most likely to act as the primary day-to-day caregiver for a patient recovering at home?

options.A: Family members living with or near the client
options.B: The contracted medical equipment delivery driver
options.C: Voluntary auditors from the federal government
options.D: The regional health commissioner on duty

explanation: That's right! In our setting, family is everything. Loved ones usually do the heavy lifting of supporting patients between our visits.

question: During early cleavage (cell division), what happens to the overall size of the cell mass?

options.A: It shrinks drastically because cells lose their water content
options.B: It grows rapidly in size as each cell feeds and expands
options.C: It flattens out into a sheet of tissue inside the tube
options.D: It stays roughly the same while cell numbers increase

explanation: Even though the cells are multiplying rapidly, they all stay snug inside the original protective shell (zona pellucida) so the total size remains similar at first.

question: What safety advice should a nurse give a patient whose vision is slightly blurred from an anti-spasmodic?

options.A: Double the next dose to build up a drug tolerance
options.B: Avoid driving or operating machinery until vision clears
options.C: Stop taking all fluids immediately to reduce swelling
options.D: Rub the eyes vigorously with a warm damp cloth

explanation: Safety first! Blurry vision makes dangerous tasks like driving a real hazard until the medication wears off.

question: What traditional mindset often drives "son preference" in many households?

options.A: Assuming that female children cannot survive childhood illnesses
options.B: Believing that girls have higher nutritional requirements than boys
options.C: Viewing boys as permanent family heirs while girls are seen as temporary members
options.D: The legal requirement that only males can inherit ancestral land

explanation: It's an old cultural bias where families invest more in boys because they carry the family name, often leaving girls shortchanged. Changing this mindset is part of our community health advocacy work!

question: Why are primary health care nurses usually the ones doing community counselling?

options.A: They are often the first point of contact for community members
options.B: They have legal authority to prescribe psychiatric drugs
options.C: They have specialized degrees in clinical psychology
options.D: They spend most of their time in large urban hospitals

explanation: Because primary care nurses work right in the community, people naturally trust them and turn to them first for help.

question: How does culture mostly shape what a family eats?

options.A: By defining which items are acceptable to eat and how meals are prepared.
options.B: By determining the exact daily caloric requirement of the human body.
options.C: By setting the official market price for imported grains.
options.D: By controlling the chemical composition of soil in the local region.

explanation: Exactly! Our cultural background teaches us from childhood what counts as good food and how it should be cooked.

question: Why does passing a urinary catheter help when managing postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: It completely stops the flow of blood from the vagina
options.B: A full bladder stops the uterus from contracting effectively
options.C: It allows the nurse to measure exact urine output
options.D: It prevents the patient from getting a urinary tract infection

explanation: An overfull bladder pushes the uterus out of place so it can't contract properly. Empty it out, and the uterus can firm up!

question: What is the main purpose of setting up youth-friendly reproductive health clinics in local communities?

options.A: To offer young people a safe, non-judgmental space to access contraception and information
options.B: To track and penalize adolescents who engage in early sexual activity
options.C: To distribute free surgical instruments for home use
options.D: To provide mandatory pregnancy testing for all high school graduates

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics take away the fear of judgment and stigma, making it easy for teenagers to ask questions and get reliable health guidance early on.

question: Why is air injected into a closed medication vial before withdrawing the liquid?

options.A: To equalize pressure and make fluid withdrawal easier
options.B: To cool down the medication temperature inside the vial
options.C: To kill any bacteria that might be living in the drug
options.D: To dilute the medication before it enters the needle

explanation: Injecting air replaces the volume of liquid being removed, preventing a vacuum from forming inside the vial which makes drawing fluid difficult. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h5)

question: How does following the Nigerian National Formulary help protect you as a nurse?

options.A: It allows them to prescribe any foreign drug without a doctor's order
options.B: It grants them the legal authority to open private retail pharmacies
options.C: It safeguards them from liability by using officially approved treatments
options.D: It exempts them from paying professional licensing renewal fees

explanation: Following approved national guidelines keeps you safe professionally. It shows you practiced according to standard, trusted nursing care!

question: What is the main body purpose of warning signs like pain and fever?

options.A: To act as warning signals indicating internal distress or disease
options.B: To punish the patient for eating unhealthy foods
options.C: To slow down normal blood circulation in the limbs
options.D: To increase the body weight of an infected person

explanation: Exactly! Think of pain and fever as the body's alarm system alerting you that something inside needs attention.

question: Which of these is NOT considered a stakeholder in a rural community immunization program?

options.A: Local religious leaders supporting health messaging
options.B: Mothers bringing their infants to the clinic
options.C: A pharmaceutical manufacturing company located overseas
options.D: Local government health department officials

explanation: Stakeholders are the people right there on the ground who care about or are affected by the program. An overseas factory making the drugs is just a distant supplier!

question: What is a common mistake nurses should avoid when suspecting a notifiable disease outbreak?

options.A: Informing the local government health team too quickly
options.B: Using standard case definition sheets during patient assessment
options.C: Waiting for full laboratory confirmation before reporting the suspect case
options.D: Submitting weekly summary logs to public health authorities

explanation: Never wait for lab results if you suspect a dangerous outbreak! Report based on clinical signs right away so health teams can act fast.

question: What is the main result of impaired drug excretion by the kidneys?

options.A: Rapid elimination of the drug through the skin
options.B: Drug accumulation and potential toxicity in the body
options.C: Immediate breakdown of the drug in the stomach
options.D: Increased therapeutic effectiveness with zero side effects

explanation: When kidneys cannot filter waste properly, drugs stay in the blood longer and build up to dangerous levels. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why is proper management of healthcare resources so important on the ward?

options.A: It stops patients from ever needing surgical interventions
options.B: It guarantees that the hospital will make a large profit
options.C: It prevents stockouts and directly protects patient safety
options.D: It eliminates the need for any nursing documentation

explanation: When we manage supplies well, the right drugs and tools are always available when a patient needs them. That avoids dangerous delays and keeps everyone safe!

question: What is the main cause of metabolic joint diseases?

options.A: Gradual loss of cartilage due to normal physical aging
options.B: Direct bacterial infection of the synovial fluid
options.C: Chemical imbalances and crystal deposits in the joints
options.D: Autoimmune attack triggered by environmental allergies

explanation: You've got this! These conditions happen when internal chemical errors cause crystals to build up in the joints, setting off painful inflammation.

question: How long does the postpartum period (puerperium) typically last?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Six months
options.C: Two weeks
options.D: Six weeks

explanation: The puerperium lasts for about six weeks (42 days) as the mother's body heals and returns to its normal, pre-pregnant state. You've got this!

question: A patient on continuous tube feeding has a red, sore spot right on the edge of their nostril. What should you do?

options.A: Clean the skin, apply a protective cream, and tape the tube to a slightly different spot
options.B: Put thick gauze padding under the tube
options.C: Leave the tape loose so the tube rubs freely
options.D: Pull the tube out permanently and stop feeding

explanation: Protecting the skin and shifting the pressure point gives the sore spot a chance to heal while keeping the patient fed.

question: How do feelings of disgust often shape food taboos in a society?

options.A: By making people lose their sense of taste completely
options.B: By increasing the body's need for protein
options.C: By associating scavenging animals with impurity and danger
options.D: By forcing individuals to eat more vegetables

explanation: When people view certain animals (like scavengers) as dirty or unsafe, that feeling of disgust turns into a long-lasting rule against eating them.

question: A patient asks why we square their height when figuring out their BMI. How should you explain it?

options.A: To adjust the weight value so it relates properly to a two-dimensional surface area
options.B: To convert the metric units into standard imperial measurements
options.C: To ensure the final number matches standard pediatric growth charts
options.D: To account for the extra weight added by heavy clothing and shoes

explanation: Well done! Squaring the height helps scale weight appropriately against body surface area rather than just a straight line measurement.

question: How do post-disaster evaluation data directly benefit future community health responses?

options.A: By guiding updates to emergency action plans and preparedness training
options.B: By proving that disasters can be completely prevented from ever happening
options.C: By reducing the number of nurses required on future hospital shifts
options.D: By eliminating the need for any future weather monitoring equipment

explanation: Learning from past mistakes allows hospitals to update their disaster plans and train staff more effectively for next time. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h8)

question: Why is family planning counseling considered such an important part of Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: It cures underlying pelvic inflammatory disease without antibiotics
options.B: It stops all immediate bleeding from uterine perforation
options.C: It helps women prevent another unwanted pregnancy in the near future
options.D: It is required by law to permanently sterilize every female patient

explanation: Spot on! Fertility returns very quickly after an abortion, so giving timely contraceptive advice helps prevent repeat unsafe procedures.

question: Which of these is a calcium channel blocker commonly prescribed for high blood pressure?

options.A: Propranolol
options.B: Verapamil
options.C: Amlodipine
options.D: Diltiazem

explanation: That's right! Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that relaxes blood vessels so blood flows more easily.

question: A patient is in the ICU after having a heart myxoma removed. What is a top nursing priority?

options.A: Encouraging heavy weightlifting to rebuild chest muscle strength
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake to zero for the first week
options.C: Monitoring continuous cardiac telemetry and vital signs
options.D: Removing the chest tubes without provider orders

explanation: After heart surgery, keeping a close eye on the heart rhythm and vital signs lets you spot and tackle complications right away. You are thinking like a real ICU nurse!

question: What is a major benefit of feeding hungry children at school?

options.A: Elimination of all infectious skin diseases
options.B: Increased physical height within one week
options.C: Guaranteed automatic promotion to the next grade
options.D: Improved concentration and classroom participation

explanation: You nailed it! A well-fed child has the brain energy needed to focus, answer questions, and join in class activities.

question: Why do anticholinergic drugs often cause annoying side effects like dry mouth and blurred vision?

options.A: They block parasympathetic nerve signals throughout the whole body
options.B: They cause a sudden drop in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: They irritate the mucous membranes in the head and neck
options.D: They dehydrate the patient by increasing kidney urine output

explanation: Because these signals help control our body's moisture and secretions, blocking them dries things up everywhere—leading to dry mouth and blurry eyes.

question: How does palliative care differ from curative care when dealing with advanced chronic illness?

options.A: Palliative care eliminates the need for any nursing or medical supervision
options.B: Palliative care focuses exclusively on performing emergency surgical procedures
options.C: Palliative care prioritizes comfort, pain control, and quality of life over curing the disease
options.D: Palliative care is only provided to patients admitted for short-term rehabilitation

explanation: Great job! When a disease can no longer be cured, palliative care shifts the focus entirely to keeping the patient comfortable, peaceful, and pain-free.

question: Which two hormones play the biggest role in helping uterine fibroids grow?

options.A: FSH and LH
options.B: Insulin and glucagon
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Estrogen and progesterone

explanation: Estrogen and progesterone fuel the growth of these muscle cells. That is why fibroids are so closely tied to a woman's reproductive years!

question: What is the best way to explain home care instructions to a patient with low health literacy?

options.A: Relying entirely on written pamphlets without verbal explanation
options.B: Using simple, plain language and asking the client to repeat instructions
options.C: Speaking in complex clinical terminology to sound professional
options.D: Handing the client a dense medical textbook to read overnight

explanation: You got it! Plain words plus the teach-back method (asking them to explain it back to you) guarantees they truly understand their treatment.

question: Why are pupil checks an essential part of the emergency neurological evaluation?

options.A: Pupil reactions tell the nurse the exact blood glucose level
options.B: They are used to measure the patient's daily fluid intake needs
options.C: They show whether the patient has an allergy to bright hospital lights
options.D: Unequal or sluggish pupils can indicate increased pressure inside the brain

explanation: Changes in pupil size and light reflex often reflect brainstem compression or intracranial pathology, serving as an early warning sign. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h6)

question: Why is proper waste management so important in a healthcare facility?

options.A: It ensures that doctors spend less time cleaning clinical wards
options.B: It prevents the facility from facing sudden financial bankruptcy

question: What is the main focus of a therapeutic nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: Meeting the social needs of the nursing staff
options.B: Building a long-lasting personal friendship
options.C: The health needs and well-being of the patient
options.D: Completing hospital paperwork as fast as possible

explanation: Well done! Unlike regular friendships, therapeutic relationships are completely focused on helping the patient get better.

question: What is the most appropriate nursing response when a dying patient expresses deep existential fear?

options.A: Telling the patient not to worry because everything is fine
options.B: Changing the subject immediately to a cheerful topic
options.C: Listening actively and validating their emotional feelings
options.D: Insisting that the patient talk to a psychiatrist today

explanation: Patients benefit most when nurses listen patiently and acknowledge their fears without dismissing them or offering false comfort. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h6)

question: How is Parkinson's disease usually diagnosed in clinical practice?

options.A: Clinical history and physical neurological examination
options.B: Routine blood tests measuring complete blood count
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis for infectious agents
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging of the spinal cord

explanation: There's no single blood test for Parkinson's! Doctors rely on a careful physical exam, watching how the patient moves, and taking a detailed medical history.

question: What life-threatening emergency can happen if a patient stops taking long-term steroids all of a sudden?

options.A: Heart attack
options.B: Malignant hypertension
options.C: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Addisonian crisis

explanation: You nailed it! Stopping steroids abruptly when the adrenal glands are inactive throws the body into a dangerous crash called an addisonian crisis.

question: What is the main focus of client-centered drug administration?

options.A: Following hospital medication schedules without exception
options.B: Leaving medication management entirely to the doctor
options.C: Reducing the time nurses spend talking to patients
options.D: Treating the patient as an active partner in their care

explanation: Client-centered care values the patient's active participation in their own treatment plan rather than treating them as a passive recipient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h1)

question: A pregnant patient at 28 weeks is tired, and tests show true iron deficiency. Where did most of her missing iron go?

options.A: Stored permanently inside the maternal liver cells
options.B: To the developing fetus and the placenta
options.C: Excreted rapidly through the gastrointestinal tract
options.D: Lost entirely through excessive maternal sweating

explanation: The growing baby always gets first priority! The baby and placenta draw a lot of iron from the mother to build their own systems.

question: A baker who develops sudden wheezing and chest tightness after inhaling flour dust at work is most likely suffering from which condition?

options.A: Asbestos-related pleural plaque
options.B: Occupational asthma
options.C: Bacterial lobar pneumonia
options.D: Coal worker's pneumoconiosis

explanation: Exposure to organic sensitizers like flour triggers an allergic airway response characterized by bronchospasm, which defines occupational asthma. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which monitoring method provides the only true proof that sterilization successfully killed all bacterial spores?

options.A: Chemical indicator tape
options.B: Visual inspection for rust
options.C: Mechanical pressure gauges
options.D: Biological indicators

explanation: Biological indicators use actual heat-resistant bacterial spores to verify that the machine successfully destroyed all microbial life. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: An experienced nurse is bored with routine duties and wants to take on hospital quality projects. What management approach fits best?

options.A: Reducing the nurse's daily patient assignment size
options.B: Focusing strictly on increasing the base hourly salary
options.C: Threatening disciplinary action for minor paperwork delays
options.D: Providing opportunities for professional achievement and growth

explanation: You nailed it! When a nurse is looking for a challenge, giving them room to grow and achieve is the best way to keep them inspired.

question: What is the main chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) released at parasympathetic target organs?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Norepinephrine
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the key messenger used by the parasympathetic system to talk to target organs. You're building a strong foundation in pharmacology and physiology!

question: What is the primary focus of the DASH diet for managing high blood pressure?

options.A: Eating plenty of fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy while reducing sodium
options.B: Eliminating all carbohydrates completely from daily meals
options.C: Eating only raw meat and root vegetables
options.D: Drinking large amounts of herbal teas and liquid supplements

explanation: The DASH diet emphasizes nutrient-dense whole foods and mineral-rich produce while cutting back on salt and unhealthy fats. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h4)

question: When MUST you use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Immediately after removing clean, non-sterile examination gloves
options.B: Before taking a patient's routine blood pressure reading
options.C: When entering a patient room for a brief verbal assessment
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Spot on! If your hands have visible dirt, blood, or body fluids on them, alcohol rubs just won't cut it. You need good old soap and water to physically wash the mess away.

question: Why do nurses carry a major responsibility in maintaining injection safety?

options.A: They purchase all medical equipment used in the healthcare facility
options.B: They are responsible for manufacturing sterile needles in the hospital
options.C: They dictate the national health policies regarding infectious waste
options.D: They are the primary healthcare workers who administer injections to patients

explanation: Nurses are directly responsible for preparing and administering injections, placing them at the center of safety protocol execution. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h1)

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations falls under which level of prevention?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Quaternary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention stops a disease or condition from occurring in the first place through measures like vaccination and health education. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why are secondary complications so dangerous for patients with brain or nerve injuries?

options.A: They can worsen the initial injury and cause further damage
options.B: They disappear without any medical intervention
options.C: They always reverse the effects of the primary disease
options.D: They only affect the peripheral nervous system

explanation: Secondary problems put extra stress on a body that is already struggling, often leading to a much worse outcome than the original injury. You've got this!

question: Why is swelling of the kidney (hydronephrosis) during pregnancy more common on the right side?

options.A: Progesterone affects the right ureter muscle fibers exclusively
options.B: The pregnant uterus typically displaces toward the right side
options.C: The right renal artery has higher blood pressure
options.D: The right kidney is anatomically larger than the left kidney

explanation: Think of the growing womb leaning slightly to the right side of the pelvis, placing direct mechanical pressure on the right tube carrying urine away from the kidney.

question: Which tool is commonly used to check distant vision during routine school health checks?

options.A: Peak flow meter
options.B: Otoscope
options.C: Sphygmomanometer
options.D: Snellen chart

explanation: You got it! The Snellen chart with rows of letters is the classic tool for checking how well school children can see from a distance.

question: Why is thorough pre-operative counseling especially critical for tubal ligation?

options.A: Patients must practice alternative birth control for six months after.
options.B: Insurance companies require psychiatric clearance before approval.
options.C: Surgeries on the reproductive system always cause permanent hormone loss.
options.D: The procedure is intended to be permanent and difficult to reverse.

explanation: Because reversal surgery is costly, complex, and has low success rates, patients must be completely certain they are finished having children before proceeding. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h3)

question: What is the main feature of an ergonomic workplace injury?

options.A: It results only from extreme cold temperatures
options.B: It develops slowly over time from repeated physical strain
options.C: It is caused by breathing in airborne bacteria
options.D: It happens instantly from an explosion or spill

explanation: Ergonomic injuries like carpal tunnel or back strain build up gradually when our bodies are subjected to poor posture and repetitive movements.

question: When is the best time for nurses to start teaching mothers about proper breastfeeding and preventing complications?

options.A: At the six-week postpartum checkup
options.B: During antenatal and early postnatal periods
options.C: Only after a breast abscess has formed
options.D: When the child is weaned to solid foods

explanation: Early teaching gives mothers the right techniques before any trouble starts. Prevention is always better than cure!

question: What is the main reason health risks must be prioritized after an assessment?

options.A: Resources and funds are always limited
options.B: The government bans solving more than one problem
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to address environmental problems
options.D: Communities never suffer from more than two health issues

explanation: We would love to fix every single problem at once, but money and time are always limited. Prioritizing helps us tackle the most urgent issues first.

question: How is Type II FGM different from Type I?

options.A: It also includes removal of the labia minora
options.B: It leaves the clitoris completely untouched
options.C: It only involves stitching the vaginal opening shut
options.D: It is performed exclusively using modern surgical lasers

question: At what angle should the head of the bed typically be elevated to help prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia?

options.A: 15 degrees downward
options.B: 90 degrees upright
options.C: 30 to 45 degrees
options.D: 0 degrees flat

explanation: Elevating the head of the bed uses gravity to stop stomach contents and oral secretions from sliding down into the lungs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why do doctors often use numbing spray and a nasal decongestant before a flexible scope goes into the nose?

options.A: To numb the passage, reduce discomfort, and shrink mucosal tissues for easier scope entry
options.B: To dilate the pupils so the patient can see the monitor during the examination
options.C: To put the patient into a deep sleep and prevent sudden body movements
options.D: To relax the heart rate and lower the patient's resting blood pressure

explanation: Spot on! The nose and throat are very sensitive, so numbing and shrinking the tissues makes the scope slide in much more comfortably.

question: Which drug class is mainly used to calm down severe leprosy reactions and save nerves from permanent damage?

options.A: Antifungal agents
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Corticosteroids
options.D: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation: Correct! Corticosteroids like prednisolone are superstars at calming down dangerous inflammation during leprosy flare-ups.

question: An older patient keeps losing their balance when standing up from the toilet. What should the nurse suggest first?

options.A: Buying a complex electronic pill dispenser
options.B: Giving them a high-dose stimulant
options.C: Moving their bedroom upstairs
options.D: Installing secure grab bars near the toilet

explanation: Safety first! Grab bars provide immediate, physical support right where they need it during risky moves like standing up.

question: What is the recommended minimum time a mother should wait before getting pregnant again, to protect her health and her child's?

options.A: Five years
options.B: One year
options.C: Six months
options.D: Two to three years

explanation: Giving at least 2 to 3 years between pregnancies lets the mother's body recover, rebuild her nutrient stores, and give the next baby a healthy start.

question: What is the very first check a nurse must perform before giving any medication?

options.A: Check the expiration date on the medication packaging
options.B: Verify the patient's identity using two unique identifiers
options.C: Ask the doctor if the prescription is still valid
options.D: Measure the patient's current vital signs

explanation: Ensuring you have the correct person is the primary safeguard in healthcare before administering any treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the route of transmission?

options.A: The time it takes for a disease to show its first symptoms
options.B: The specific path a pathogen takes from its source to a new host
options.C: The total number of microbes required to cause an infection
options.D: The chemical makeup of an infectious agent's outer shell

explanation: The route of transmission is simply the way a germ travels from where it lives to a person who can catch it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h1)

question: Why does the body form small bumps called granulomas during a TB infection?

options.A: To help transport oxygen across damaged alveolar membranes
options.B: To produce antibodies that neutralize the bacterial toxins
options.C: To wall off and contain the bacteria within the lungs
options.D: To stimulate rapid production of red blood cells

explanation: Think of granulomas as a smart defensive wall built by your immune system to trap the TB germs so they cannot wander around your lungs.

question: Why is a change in mental status often the first sign of developing shock?

options.A: Brain tissue is extremely sensitive to reductions in oxygen and blood supply
options.B: Fluid overload in the bloodstream causes immediate brain swelling
options.C: Pain receptors in the skin send distress signals to the brain
options.D: Anxiety releases hormones that directly cause kidney failure

explanation: The brain has high metabolic demands and reacts quickly when oxygen delivery drops, making confusion or restlessness an early alarm bell. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why is an unsteady walk (gait instability) such a big worry for patients with nerve degeneration?

options.A: It prevents the patient from speaking clearly
options.B: It triggers sudden spikes in blood pressure
options.C: It greatly increases the risk of dangerous falls and injury
options.D: It causes immediate permanent blindness in both eyes

explanation: When balance is off, walking safely becomes a daily challenge. As nurses, keeping our patients safe from falls is a huge priority!

question: If a newly discovered hormone passes right through cell membranes without needing a surface receptor, what is it likely made of?

options.A: Large peptide
options.B: Water-soluble amine
options.C: Protein hormone
options.D: Steroid hormone

explanation: Fat likes fat! Because steroid hormones are lipid-soluble, they slide smoothly across the fatty cell membrane to reach receptors inside. Brilliant deduction!

question: What main effect does digoxin have on the heart?

options.A: It speeds up electrical conduction through all nodes
options.B: It removes excess body water through the kidneys
options.C: It relaxes the coronary arteries to increase blood flow
options.D: It increases contraction force and slows heart rate

explanation: Digoxin is fascinating! It acts like a double agent: it makes each squeeze stronger, but slows down the overall heart rate so the heart can rest and fill properly.

question: What is the purpose of conducting routine preventive maintenance on hospital backup generators?

options.A: To ensure uninterrupted power for critical life-support equipment during outages
options.B: To replace all the lighting fixtures in the administrative offices annually
options.C: To lower the daily electricity bill charged by the public utility company
options.D: To increase the speed at which elevators transport patients between floors

explanation: When public power fails, backup generators must kick in instantly to keep life-saving machines like ventilators running smoothly. Regular checks make sure they never let us down!

question: Why must nurses monitor a patient's blood pressure closely after they get spinal anesthesia?

options.A: Pain medication given intrathecally always increases heart rate
options.B: Lying flat naturally causes sudden spikes in blood pressure
options.C: The body always produces extra blood volume after a spinal injection
options.D: Local anesthetics can block sympathetic nerves and cause significant low blood pressure

explanation: Spot on! Spinal meds can affect the nerves that keep your blood vessels tight, leading to a sudden drop in blood pressure that we need to catch early.

question: Why do modern nursing units often prefer a flat organizational structure?

options.A: It empowers frontline nurses to make quicker decisions
options.B: It removes the need for any nurse managers or supervisors
options.C: It guarantees that every patient has a private room
options.D: It completely stops nurses from ever working night shifts

explanation: Exactly! Cutting out too many layers of management helps nurses act faster and talk directly with leaders when patient needs arise.

question: Which regulatory body sets the professional and legal standards for nursing practice and documentation in Nigeria?

options.A: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

options.D: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare

question: In the famous 'CAUTION' warning signs of cancer, what does the letter 'U' stand for?

options.A: Unexplained weight gain
options.B: Urinary tract infection
options.C: Unusual bleeding or discharge
options.D: Ulceration of the skin

explanation: Remember CAUTION! The 'U' reminds us to never ignore unexplained bleeding or discharge from any part of the body. Keep that in your nursing toolkit!

question: Which part of the brain acts as the direct link between the nervous system and the endocrine system?

options.A: Thalamus
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Hypothalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The hypothalamus is the master bridge! It takes nervous system signals and translates them into hormonal commands for the pituitary gland.

question: What is a major problem when a hospital is run using fear and intimidation?

options.A: Staff members tend to hide errors and near-misses out of self-protection.
options.B: The hospital saves money on incident report paperwork.
options.C: Nurses become eager to report every small documentation typo.

explanation: When people are terrified of punishment, they sweep mistakes under the rug—which means the team loses a chance to learn and keep future patients safe.

question: What is considered the primary patient for a public health nurse?

options.A: The physician in charge
options.B: The entire community
options.C: The hospitalized individual
options.D: The critically ill patient

explanation: Unlike clinical nurses who care for single patients at the bedside, public health nurses focus on populations and communities as a whole. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h1)

question: If a local government wants to reduce rabies cases in humans, what should they prioritize first?

options.A: Draining all local ponds and slow-moving irrigation streams
options.B: Conducting a mass vaccination campaign for domestic dogs
options.C: Providing free insecticide-treated nets to market traders
options.D: Issuing strict travel bans on all livestock transport vehicles

explanation: Brilliant! Since dogs are the main carrier of rabies, vaccinating them directly protects us from exposure.

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks is worried because a little yellowish fluid is leaking from her nipples. As a nurse, what do you tell her?

options.A: This means labor is likely to begin within the next forty-eight hours

question: A nurse wants to show the percentage breakdown of different nursing specialties in a hospital. Which chart should be used?

options.A: Pie chart
options.B: Line graph

options.D: Histogram

question: How is andropause in men different from menopause in women?

options.C: Symptoms only appear before the age of thirty in men

explanation: Unlike female menopause which brings a relatively sharp stop to monthly cycles, male hormone levels drop slowly and steadily over many years.

question: What is the primary goal of secondary prevention strategies for a patient?

options.A: Preventing any future contact between the host and the environment
options.B: Rehabilitating a patient after permanent disability has occurred
options.C: Eliminating the vector species completely from a tropical region
options.D: Detecting and treating an infection early before it causes severe illness

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching things early! Think of screenings and prompt treatments that stop a small infection from turning into a major emergency.

question: What is a common barrier to tele-nursing in rural areas?

options.A: Strict government laws banning telephone conversations
options.B: Digital illiteracy and lack of modern devices
options.C: An excess of high-end personal computers in every home
options.D: Patients refusing care because they live too close to clinics

question: Which of these is a great example of the teach-back method in action?

options.A: Is there anything confusing about taking two tablets every morning?

options.C: Can you read this pamphlet out loud to prove your vision is fine?
options.D: Show me how you plan to use your blood glucose meter before you leave today.

question: What is the main goal of having a multi-sectoral referral network for GBV survivors?

options.A: To provide comprehensive medical, legal, and social support through coordinated agencies
options.B: To reduce the total number of follow-up medical visits required
options.C: To transfer all administrative responsibilities away from the hospital
options.D: To ensure the police handle every aspect of the patient's recovery

explanation: Healing takes a village! Teamwork between health workers, legal aid, and social services gives survivors the best all-round support.

question: How do secondary bone tumors differ from primary bone tumors?

options.A: Secondary tumors originate strictly from bone marrow cells
options.B: Secondary tumors are always benign growths that stop growing early
options.C: Secondary tumors only affect the cartilage and never the hard bone
options.D: Secondary tumors spread to the bone from another organ in the body

explanation: Think of secondary tumors as travellers. They started somewhere else like the breast or prostate and hitchhiked to the bones.

question: Why must nurses ask patients about their family planning or contraceptive methods?

options.A: To replace the need for asking about sexual partners
options.B: To judge the personal lifestyle choices of the patient
options.C: To evaluate pregnancy prevention methods and potential hormone side effects
options.D: To determine how much tax the patient pays

explanation: No judgment here—just good nursing! Asking about contraception helps us understand cycle changes, check for side effects, and support the patient's family goals.

question: What is the main goal of sitting down for pre-test counselling with a patient?

options.A: To prepare the client for the test and discuss risk reduction
options.B: To administer the antiretroviral medication immediately
options.C: To force the client to reveal all past sexual partners
options.D: To collect mandatory employment data for the government

explanation: Exactly! Pre-test talks help check if the client is ready, explain how the test works, and chat about staying safe.

question: What is fundal height measurement used for during pregnancy?

options.A: To check the mother's baseline blood pressure
options.B: To calculate the total weight the mother will gain
options.C: To screen the mother for gestational diabetes
options.D: To estimate gestational age and fetal growth

explanation: Measuring from the pubic bone to the uterine top helps nurses track how well the baby is growing week by week. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h3)

question: Why do fast-moving essential medicines usually have lower mark-up percentages in a DRF?

options.A: To ensure maximum affordability and access for high-volume treatments
options.B: Because they never expire or suffer from stock damage
options.C: Because they are cheaper for the manufacturer to produce
options.D: To discourage patients from buying them in large quantities

explanation: Exactly! Keeping high-demand medicines cheap protects everyday patients and ensures a fast turnover of stock, which keeps cash flowing steadily back into the fund.

question: Which leadership style works best with the core philosophy of team nursing?

options.A: Democratic leadership involving mutual respect
options.B: Strict autocratic control by auxiliary staff
options.C: Total absence of leadership or direction
options.D: Remote management from outside the hospital

explanation: Well done! Team nursing thrives when the leader respects every member and encourages collaboration instead of just barking harsh commands. Great ward dynamics!

question: Why do nurses need to look at social services alongside medical care?

options.A: Medical treatments are completely ineffective without prior social assessment.
options.B: Patient recovery and well-being depend heavily on social and economic factors outside the hospital.
options.C: Nurses are legally required to distribute government welfare grants directly.
options.D: Hospital management mandates that nurses handle all community social work.

explanation: Medical care is only one piece of the puzzle! Factors like a patient's home, income, and community support play a massive role in how well and how fast they heal.

question: Why are advance directives so helpful in critical or end-of-life care?

options.A: They guarantee that the patient will recover fully
options.B: They guide medical treatment according to the patient's prior wishes
options.C: They eliminate all paperwork for the hospital staff
options.D: They give the doctor total control over all decisions

explanation: Advance directives let patients make their choices known ahead of time, taking the guesswork out of difficult situations.

question: What is a 'status offense'?

options.A: An act that is illegal only because the person is a minor
options.B: Any offense that results in immediate capital punishment
options.C: A minor traffic violation committed by a licensed driver
options.D: A violent crime committed by an adult against a child

explanation: You're doing great! A status offense is an action that is only breaking the rule because of the offender's young age—like skipping school or running away from home.

question: What makes a modern modular operating theatre special in terms of structure?

options.A: Seamless, pre-fabricated panels that resist bacterial growth
options.B: Wooden flooring to absorb sound and reduce echoes
options.C: Traditional painted concrete walls that are easy to repaint
options.D: Open windows to allow natural sunlight during daytime surgery

explanation: Spot on! Modular theatres use smooth, factory-made panels so there are no tiny cracks or corners where stubborn germs and dust can hide.

question: Why do many FGM survivors hesitate to speak up about their sexual and mental struggles?

options.A: Psychological symptoms disappear completely after marriage
options.B: Cultural taboos make discussing female sexuality difficult
options.C: Hospitals routinely provide mandatory counseling at birth
options.D: Mental health professionals are legally banned from treating women

explanation: Strict societal taboos around sex and reproductive parts force many women to hide their pain and suffer in silence. As a nurse, your gentle care creates a safe space for them.

question: A patient with a stroke in the front of the pons is fully awake and alert, but cannot speak or move their body below the neck. What is this called?

options.A: Brown-Séquard syndrome
options.B: Horner syndrome

question: What do we mean by Post-Ebola Syndrome?

options.B: A permanent mental illness from the incubation period
options.C: An acute respiratory infection before fever starts
options.D: A sudden relapse of active internal bleeding on day two

explanation: You got it! Even after beating the virus, survivors can deal with lingering joint pain, fatigue, and vision issues.

question: Why is it helpful to view drug addiction as a public health disease rather than a moral failure?

options.A: It encourages affected individuals to seek medical treatment earlier without fear
options.B: It allows the government to stop all funding for local hospitals
options.C: It guarantees that prescription drugs will become free for everyone
options.D: It stops people from ever feeling sad or stressed in life

explanation: Stigma makes people hide their struggles. Treating addiction as a medical issue helps patients come forward for help proudly and early.

question: You just finished explaining how to mix oral rehydration salts to a father. What is the best next step?

options.A: Send him home immediately to start treatment without checking
options.B: Assume he understood because he nodded his head politely
options.C: Ask the father to demonstrate how he will mix the solution
options.D: Give him a written quiz with difficult multiple-choice questions

explanation: Spot on! Having him show you right away is the best practical way to ensure he really understood and can do it at home.

question: Why does the structural difference between gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria matter in pharmacology?

options.A: It dictates the correct storage temperature for oral medications
options.B: It determines how fast a patient's kidneys filter out IV fluids
options.C: It explains why certain bacterial types are harder to treat with specific drugs
options.D: It tells the nurse exactly how many calories the patient needs daily

question: Why can transitioning from a hospital to home care be tough for a nurse?

options.A: Hospitals use entirely different medical terminology.
options.B: Hospitals do not teach any clinical procedures.
options.C: Home care requires autonomous decision-making without immediate medical backup.
options.D: Nurses in hospitals never interact with patients directly.

question: Which important hormone does the placenta make to keep early pregnancy going strong?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: This is the famous hormone (hCG) detected by pregnancy tests! It signals the body to protect the pregnancy during those crucial first few weeks.

question: A patient is leaving the hospital after treatment for a deep fungal infection. Which oral azole is commonly used for long-term follow-up care?

options.A: Nystatin
options.B: Amphotericin B
options.C: Caspofungin
options.D: Fluconazole
