question: Where in the brain is the main control center for the cough reflex located?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Spinal cord
options.C: Frontal lobe
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The medulla oblongata is the brainstem command center that coordinates the whole physical action of coughing.

question: What is the primary underlying cause of coronary artery disease?

options.A: Inflammation of the outer sac surrounding the heart
options.B: Dilation and weakening of the heart muscle walls
options.C: Sudden infection of the inner heart lining
options.D: Buildup of fatty plaque inside the coronary arteries

explanation: Coronary artery disease develops primarily when cholesterol and other fats form plaque inside the arteries supplying the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h1)

question: What do we mean by environmental factors in education?

options.A: External conditions and influences shaping the educational experience
options.B: Strictly the financial cost of attending a nursing program
options.C: Only the physical temperature inside a traditional classroom
options.D: The genetic makeup and natural intelligence of the student

explanation: Environmental factors cover all outside elements that impact how you learn, from your physical surroundings to your support systems. You've got this!

question: What is a very common local belief about injected medications compared to pills?

options.A: Pills are absorbed directly into the bloodstream
options.B: Pills are always more expensive than injections
options.C: Injections have zero risk of side effects
options.D: Injections are believed to work faster and more powerfully

explanation: That's right! Many people hold the myth that injections are stronger magic because they go straight into the body.

question: A nurse needs to inform the shift team about a new hospital policy change. What is the best way to use group communication for this?

options.A: Send a secure group message or email to all staff members on the ward
options.B: Write the policy on a random patient whiteboard in the main hallway
options.C: Share the details on a personal social media account without privacy filters
options.D: Call every single staff member individually during their busy morning rounds

explanation: Group messaging allows charge nurses to efficiently broadcast general updates and policy changes to an entire team at once. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why is knowing the exact date of a patient's last menstrual period (LMP) so important?

options.A: It proves the patient has reached full menopause
options.B: It establishes a baseline for dating a pregnancy or spotting cycle changes
options.C: It indicates the exact day ovulation will occur next month
options.D: It measures the total amount of iron stored in the blood

explanation: You will use this all the time in clinic! The LMP helps us calculate expected due dates for pregnant mums and spot any unusual bleeding patterns early.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to keep a stakeholder coalition strong and unified?

options.A: Mutual respect for different contributions
options.B: Clear roles for all participating members
options.C: Ignoring opposing views within the coalition
options.D: Transparent communication among groups

explanation: Spot on! Brushing opposing views under the rug destroys trust. A strong coalition needs open communication and respect for everyone's opinions.

question: An activity coordinator plans a group exercise session. Which client adaptation best demonstrates person-centered care?

options.A: Excusing clients from participating if they look tired once
options.B: Requiring all clients to stand and follow the exact same routine
options.C: Skipping physical exercise altogether for safety reasons
options.D: Providing seated chair exercises for clients with poor balance

explanation: Adapting activities to individual functional levels, such as offering seated options, ensures safe and inclusive participation for everyone. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h5)

question: What should you do immediately if a laboring patient's cervical dilation plot crosses over the action line?

options.A: The nurse should switch from intravenous fluids to oral clear broths
options.B: The patient is ready for immediate spontaneous vaginal delivery at home
options.C: All monitoring can be safely stopped for the next six hours
options.D: Immediate medical evaluation and intervention are required

explanation: Crossing the action line means labour is taking longer than expected. It's your cue to get the doctor involved right away so mother and baby stay safe.

question: What do we call a sudden poisoning that happens right after a person has one large exposure to a chemical?

options.A: Acute exposure
options.B: Chronic exposure
options.C: Dermal accumulation
options.D: Systemic absorption

explanation: You've got this! Acute exposure simply means a one-time, short contact with a substance that quickly leads to symptoms or harm. Think of it as a sudden event, unlike chronic exposure which builds up over a long time.

question: What is a major difference between paracetamol (acetaminophen) and NSAIDs?

options.A: Acetaminophen causes significant gastric bleeding
options.B: NSAIDs work exclusively inside the spinal cord
options.C: NSAIDs have no effect on body temperature
options.D: Acetaminophen lacks peripheral anti-inflammatory action

explanation: Both lower fever and ease pain, but paracetamol doesn't fight body inflammation or affect bleeding the way NSAIDs do.

question: Why must acids and alkaline substances (bases) never be stored right next to each other?

options.A: Mixing them can cause violent reactions, heat, or toxic gas
options.B: Alkaline fumes destroy the paper labels on acid containers
options.C: They will neutralize each other and become expensive perfume
options.D: Acids make alkaline bottles shrink and leak everywhere

explanation: Spot on! Acids and bases react strongly when they meet, often releasing dangerous heat, splashes, or poisonous fumes. Keeping them apart keeps everyone safe.

question: Which patient is the best candidate for a routine fasting blood sugar screening?

options.A: A young child recovering from a normal cold
options.B: A healthy athlete with mild muscle soreness after running
options.C: An adult with obesity and a family history of diabetes
options.D: An elderly patient admitted with a broken bone from a fall

explanation: Great thinking! People with risk factors like extra weight and a family history are prime candidates for routine checks so we catch issues early.

question: Which part of the brain acts as the master control center to start the menstrual cycle?

options.A: The adrenal gland
options.B: The thyroid gland
options.C: The pituitary gland
options.D: The hypothalamus

explanation: Think of the hypothalamus as the head office in the brain—it sends the very first signal (GnRH) to kick off the cycle!

question: What is a major benefit of involving community health workers in post-abortion care programs?

options.A: They manufacture affordable modern contraceptives locally
options.B: They replace doctors and nurses in urban teaching hospitals
options.C: They help educate the public and guide women to facilities early
options.D: They perform surgical manual vacuum aspirations in rural homes

explanation: You got it! Community workers are vital links who spot danger signs early and direct women to get proper medical help.

question: What is one of the biggest challenges nurses face when taking skinfold measurements?

options.A: Variations in technique between nurses can lead to inconsistent results
options.B: It is impossible to perform on patients who are conscious
options.C: The test causes permanent bruising at the anatomical site
options.D: The equipment requires a continuous electrical power source

explanation: You got it! Skinfold testing takes practice. If two different nurses pinch slightly different spots or angles, they might get different readings.

question: What is the main difference between a communicable disease and a non-communicable disease?

options.A: It cannot be treated with standard medications
options.B: It is always caused by a genetic mutation
options.C: It only affects people living in urban areas
options.D: It can be transmitted from a reservoir to a susceptible host

explanation: You've got this! Communicable diseases can spread from one person or source to another, unlike chronic conditions like hypertension.

question: Where does fertilization of the human egg normally happen?

options.A: In the ampulla of the fallopian tube
options.B: Along the lower third of the myometrium
options.C: Directly inside the uterine cavity
options.D: Within the peritoneal cavity of the pelvis

explanation: Spot on! The sperm and egg usually meet in the widest part of the fallopian tube, called the ampulla, before starting their trip to the uterus. You've got this!

question: How should you support a joint while doing passive range of motion exercises?

options.A: Placing your hands above and below the joint
options.B: Letting the limb dangle freely without support
options.C: Holding the joint tightly right at its center point
options.D: Pulling firmly on the fingers or toes

explanation: Great job! Cradling the joint with hands positioned above and below gives solid support and protects the surrounding tissue.

question: What is the most common nutritional shortage that causes microcytic anaemia?

options.A: Protein shortage
options.B: Vitamin C lack
options.C: Iron deficiency
options.D: Calcium deficiency

explanation: Great to know for clinicals! Without enough iron, the body cannot build proper hemoglobin, leaving red blood cells looking small and pale.

question: A patient is experiencing acute withdrawal tremors and confusion. Which nursing diagnosis should be your top priority?

options.A: Ineffective Health Maintenance
options.B: Chronic Low Self-Esteem
options.C: Deficient Fluid Volume
options.D: Risk for Injury

explanation: Correct! With tremors and confusion, keeping the patient safe from falls, seizures, and self-harm is always the absolute first priority in nursing care.

question: Why is getting the right specimen so important for prescribing antibiotics?

options.A: It allows doctors to prescribe targeted therapy rather than guessing
options.B: It prevents nurses from needing to wear sterile gloves
options.C: It ensures the patient receives the strongest drug available immediately
options.D: It lowers the financial cost of hospital room maintenance

explanation: When we know the exact bug, the doctor can give the right drug instead of just guessing. That stops antibiotic resistance and helps the patient heal faster!

question: What is the main goal of Psychological First Aid (PFA) during an emergency?

options.A: Providing practical care and emotional support
options.B: Diagnosing long-term mental health disorders
options.C: Replacing professional psychiatric therapy
options.D: Forcing survivors to recount trauma details

explanation: You've got this! PFA is simply about showing up with practical help and a comforting presence—not digging into deep therapy or forcing anyone to retell painful stories.

question: Why does an undescended testicle have a higher risk of developing cancer later in life?

options.A: Constant friction against the pelvic bones triggers rapid cell division
options.B: The lack of hormones from the pituitary gland causes cell mutation
options.C: Blood flow to the testicle is normally twice as high in the abdomen
options.D: Higher body heat inside the abdomen damages the cells over time

explanation: The scrotum is naturally cooler, which sperm cells love. The warmer temperature inside the abdomen can harm these cells over time and raise cancer risks.

question: When a client wants to switch to a different birth control method during a follow-up visit, what is your main job as a nurse?

options.A: Charge an extra administrative fee for changing the care plan
options.B: Refuse service until a senior medical officer approves the change
options.C: Force the client to continue the original method for at least one more year
options.D: Ensure there is no gap in contraceptive coverage to prevent unintended pregnancy

explanation: When changing methods, timing is everything. We must make sure there is no unprotected gap where an unintended pregnancy could happen.

question: What is the main purpose of medication reconciliation during a patient admission?

options.A: Determining which pharmaceutical company manufactured the prescribed drugs
options.B: Disposing of all expired herbal medicines found in the patient bedside locker
options.C: Calculating the total financial cost of drugs used during hospital admission
options.D: Creating an accurate list of all current medications to prevent errors

explanation: Medication reconciliation ensures healthcare providers have an accurate, complete picture of every substance the patient is taking. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h4)

question: About how many centimeters is the diaphragm pushed upward during pregnancy?

options.A: Twelve centimeters
options.B: One centimeter
options.C: Four centimeters
options.D: Ten centimeters

explanation: As the baby grows, the uterus pushes the diaphragm up by about four centimeters, making the rib cage widen out to give the lungs space. Keep going!

question: What is the big difference between organ-specific and systemic autoimmune diseases?

options.A: Systemic conditions are caused exclusively by viral infections
options.B: Systemic diseases only affect the skin, while organ-specific affect the brain
options.C: Organ-specific conditions cannot be treated with medication
options.D: Organ-specific targets a single tissue, while systemic affects multiple organs

explanation: Organ-specific focuses its attack on just one place (like the thyroid), while systemic conditions cause widespread chaos across many parts of the body.

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for maintaining the male accessory glands?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Testosterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Androgens like testosterone control the structure and secretory activity of the accessory reproductive glands. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is considered the gold-standard, first-choice treatment for chronic insomnia?

options.A: High-dose benzodiazepines every night
options.B: Complete sensory deprivation therapy
options.C: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I)
options.D: Over-the-counter antihistamines

explanation: CBT-I is the top recommendation! It helps retrain your brain and sleep habits for long-term success without any risk of drug dependence.

question: According to the Transtheoretical Model, what is the very first stage of behavioural change?

options.A: Preparation
options.B: Maintenance
options.C: Action
options.D: Precontemplation

explanation: Correct! In the precontemplation stage, a person isn't thinking about changing yet, and might not even see that there is a problem.

question: Why is drinking enough water important for protecting a susceptible host?

options.A: It directly destroys bacterial cell walls in the bloodstream
options.B: It replaces the need for standard vaccinations
options.C: It permanently eliminates all body toxins
options.D: It keeps mucosal membranes moist to trap foreign particles

explanation: Simple and natural! Well-hydrated mucous membranes in your nose and throat act like sticky traps to catch germs before they enter.

question: As a nurse, what is the best first step before handing out a sleeping pill?

options.A: Checking the patient's visual acuity in bright sunlight
options.B: Administering a cup of strong coffee to test drug interactions
options.C: Requiring the patient to sign a legal release form
options.D: Assessing the underlying cause of insomnia and trying sleep hygiene measures

explanation: Always check why they can't sleep and try natural comfort tips first before reaching straight for the prescription pad!

question: Why is it so important to ask about a client's last menstrual period before starting birth control?

options.A: To check if the client has an active sexually transmitted infection
options.B: To calculate the exact date of menopause the client will experience
options.C: To reasonably rule out an existing, early pregnancy before starting birth control
options.D: To determine how many children the client has delivered in the past

explanation: Spot on! We always want to be sure a client isn't already pregnant before starting certain contraceptives to keep both her and the early pregnancy safe.

question: Which common group of over-the-counter pain relievers is a major cause of peptic ulcers?

options.A: Broad-spectrum oral antifungal agents
options.B: First-generation antihistamine pills
options.C: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.D: Fat-soluble multivitamin supplements

explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen block protective chemicals in the stomach lining, making it super easy for acid to cause damage.

question: Why do lab staff test new batches of agar plates using known, trusted strains of bacteria?

options.A: To prove that all bacteria can survive without any oxygen
options.B: To confirm the media supports proper microbial growth
options.C: To measure the exact room temperature of the building
options.D: To clean the interior glass walls of the laboratory incubator

explanation: Quality control is key! Testing the plates beforehand makes sure our materials are in top shape before real patient samples arrive.

question: In professional nursing, what does 'responsibility' actually mean?

options.A: The personal ability to influence others without holding a title
options.B: The official legal right to command subordinate workers
options.C: The financial reward given for working extra night shifts
options.D: The obligation to perform assigned tasks and achieve expected results

explanation: Think of responsibility as your professional duty—it's the commitment to get your assigned nursing tasks done properly and safely!

question: Why must a nurse collect a wound culture BEFORE giving the first dose of a new antibiotic?

options.A: Starting the drug first will completely destroy all local laboratory equipment
options.B: Laboratory regulations require paperwork to be filed prior to dosing
options.C: Pre-dosing culture collection is only required for oral medications
options.D: The medication can alter bacteria levels and mask the true infection source

explanation: If you give the drug first, it might kill off or hide the bacteria in the sample, giving the lab a false-negative result. Always swab first, treat second!

question: Which animal serves as the natural home or reservoir for the Lassa virus?

options.A: Cow
options.B: Mosquito
options.C: Domestic cat
options.D: Multimammate rat

explanation: Exactly! The multimammate rat carries the Lassa virus and sheds it in its urine and droppings, which can accidentally contaminate our food.

question: What simple comfort measure can a nurse suggest for a patient dealing with dry mouth from these drugs?

options.A: Take small sips of water often or suck on sugarless sweets
options.B: Stop drinking all fluids for the rest of the day
options.C: Take your medication right before doing heavy exercise
options.D: Rinse your mouth with strong salt water every single hour

explanation: Brilliant nursing care! Frequent sips of water or sugarless candy keep those mucous membranes nice and comfortable without messing with their blood sugar.

question: Why is staying stuck at home a big concern for patients with physical disabilities?

options.A: It cuts them off from regular religious and social community gatherings
options.B: It guarantees that they will develop a severe nutritional deficiency
options.C: It prevents community health nurses from visiting their homes
options.D: It automatically stops their prescription medication deliveries

explanation: Mobility barriers can trap people at home, isolating them from their places of worship and friends. Community support makes a huge difference!

question: What does a holistic approach mean in palliative care?

options.A: Addressing physical, emotional, and spiritual needs together
options.B: Focusing exclusively on spiritual counseling
options.C: Relying entirely on herbal remedies and local roots
options.D: Treating only the physical pain of the patient

explanation: A holistic approach looks at the *whole* person—body, mind, and spirit. We don't just treat a sore body; we care for the heart and mind too!

question: How does poor hospital infrastructure affect a nurse's daily shift?

options.A: It forces nurses to spend more time improvising care due to missing tools
options.B: It guarantees that nurses will receive higher hazard allowances
options.C: It reduces the total number of patients seeking medical attention
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for patient documentation

explanation: Nigerian nurses are masters of improvisation! When basic equipment is missing, you have to think on your feet to keep patients safe. That takes true skill.

question: Which symptom should a nurse teach a patient with dysmenorrhoea to report immediately?

options.A: Feeling tired and needing extra sleep during bleeding
options.B: Mild lower abdominal cramping on the first day of menses
options.C: Sudden high fever and foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.D: A slight decrease in appetite during the menstrual cycle

explanation: You got it! Fever and foul discharge are red flags for an infection, which means it's not just regular period pain and needs urgent attention.

question: In research language, what is a 'sampling frame'?

options.A: A framework for writing up the final research report
options.B: The physical room where patient interviews take place
options.C: A complete list of everyone in the accessible population
options.D: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size

explanation: Think of a sampling frame as your phone book or registry list. It's the actual directory of names you draw your participants from!

question: What physiological event occurs during the resolution phase of the sexual response cycle?

options.A: Involuntary rhythmic muscle contractions begin across the pelvis
options.B: Blood pressure and heart rate reach their absolute peak levels
options.C: Pelvic blood flow increases rapidly to prepare for orgasm
options.D: The body gradually returns to its unaroused baseline state

explanation: During resolution, physiological parameters like heart rate and blood flow return to normal non-stimulated levels. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h2)

question: During birth, the baby's chin tucks tightly against its chest. What is this movement called?

options.A: Flexion
options.B: Extension
options.C: Descent
options.D: Restitution

explanation: That tucking action is called flexion! It helps the smallest part of the baby's head lead the way through the pelvis.

question: Which nursing practice is widely known as the most effective way to stop infections from spreading in hospitals?

options.A: Painting hospital walls with bright colors
options.B: Regular and thorough hand hygiene
options.C: Replacing all cotton uniforms with nylon
options.D: Closing the outpatient department daily at noon

explanation: Spot on! Simple, consistent handwashing remains our absolute best defense against spreading healthcare-associated infections.

question: What is the main reason infectious waste is shredded after going through microwave treatment?

options.A: To render the waste unrecognizable and reduce its physical volume
options.B: To reactivate dormant bacterial spores for laboratory testing
options.C: To separate plastic components from metal parts manually
options.D: To increase the weight of the bags before final transport

explanation: Shredding ensures nobody can scavenge or reuse treated medical items, and it shrinks the trash down so it's easier to haul away to a landfill.

question: Which of these activities is a great example of 'mutual aid'?

options.A: Neighbors contributing money to pay for a sick person's hospital bill
options.B: A police officer giving a traffic ticket to a speeding driver
options.C: A commercial bank approving a business loan for a farmer
options.D: A teacher giving a graded examination to students in a school

explanation: Spot on! Mutual aid happens when community members voluntarily join hands to support someone who is sick or in need.

question: Which of the following is considered a vector in disease transmission?

options.A: A shared towel
options.B: A contaminated well
options.C: A mosquito
options.D: A surgical scalpel

explanation: Mosquitoes are living organisms that actively transmit disease agents like malaria parasites between hosts, making them classic biological vectors. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why must broad-spectrum antibiotics be given right away to a patient with a septic incomplete abortion?

options.A: To directly stimulate uterine contractions and expel retained tissue
options.B: To control and prevent the spread of ascending bacterial infection and septic shock
options.C: To replace lost blood volume and increase hemoglobin levels
options.D: To lower systemic blood pressure and reduce anxiety

explanation: Unsterile procedures let bacteria into the uterus, which can quickly spread into the blood and cause deadly septic shock. Quick antibiotics are life-savers!

question: What is the main way that most foodborne germs get into our bodies?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Fecal-oral route
options.C: Direct sexual contact
options.D: Airborne droplet route

explanation: It sounds unpleasant, but tiny, microscopic traces of waste pathogens find their way onto food or water and enter right through the mouth. Handwashing is our best defense!

question: Why is overfilling a sharps safety box a dangerous hazard?

options.A: It prevents the incineration machine from burning paper waste
options.B: It increases the chemical weight of the plastic container
options.C: It automatically dissolves the cardboard exterior
options.D: It exposes handlers and cleaners to protruding needles

explanation: Overfilled boxes mean needles are sticking out, ready to accidentally prick anyone who handles or carries them. Close and replace those boxes before they get too full!

question: When does bereavement support typically begin and end in a hospice program?

options.A: It begins only after one full year has passed
options.B: It continues for months after the patient passes away
options.C: It only occurs during the final week of the patient's life
options.D: It stops immediately the moment the patient dies

explanation: Bereavement care is an ongoing service that supports grieving family members for many months following their loss. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h8)

question: A community nurse meets resistance from male elders who think family planning promotes promiscuity. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the elders completely and hand out contraceptives secretly behind their backs
options.B: Engage the men in respectful dialogue, emphasizing child spacing, maternal health, and family financial stability
options.C: Argue with them aggressively to prove that their traditional beliefs are entirely wrong
options.D: Report the entire village community to the local police station immediately

explanation: Community health nursing requires patience and respect. Sitting down to talk with community leaders helps frame family planning around health, peace, and family well-being.

question: Which part of the brain is responsible for releasing Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)?

options.A: The hypothalamus
options.B: The cerebral cortex
options.C: The cerebellum
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: You got it! The hypothalamus acts as the master control center in the brain, pulsing out GnRH to kickstart reproductive development.

question: Why does a drop in local currency value make medications so much more expensive?

options.A: Doctors start prescribing more expensive brands
options.B: Governments place heavy taxes on local pharmacies
options.C: Many essential drugs and raw materials are imported
options.D: Local factories stop producing tablets entirely

explanation: Spot on! Because we import a lot of our medicines and raw ingredients, a weaker currency means it costs much more to bring them into the country.

question: Who is the focus of Tier 4 at the peak of the MHPSS pyramid?

options.A: Individuals with severe, disabling mental health conditions
options.B: Community volunteers organizing children's playgroups
options.C: People who simply need help finding food and clean water
options.D: Everyone living in a disaster-affected community

explanation: You're correct! Tier 4 is reserved for the smaller group of people who need specialized psychiatric care for severe mental health conditions.

question: Why do we use a Gram stain when looking at a bacterial colony under the microscope?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the bacterial sample on a scale
options.B: To freeze the microorganisms so they can be stored for years
options.C: To provide extra nutrients for the bacteria to grow faster
options.D: To categorize the bacteria by their cell wall structure and color

explanation: Gram staining is a classic nursing and lab trick! It sorts bacteria into neat groups based on how their cell walls react to the violet dye.

question: What is a common long-term effect of eating too many trans and saturated fats?

options.A: Atherosclerosis and higher heart risk
options.B: Stronger storage of vitamins in bones
options.C: Less inflammation in the arteries
options.D: Better production of good cholesterol

explanation: Eating too many bad fats causes fatty plaque to build up in the arteries (atherosclerosis), making the heart work much harder. Good catch!

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when turning an annoying ward problem into a research question?

options.A: Ordering expensive laboratory equipment for the ward
options.B: Reporting the nursing staff to the hospital board
options.C: Writing a textbook about the clinical problem
options.D: Focusing the observation onto clear, measurable variables

explanation: Start by breaking down your general frustration into specific pieces you can actually observe, count, or measure in the ward.

question: What is a major systemic challenge frequently facing primary health care centers in Nigeria today?

options.A: Too many operational hospitals with zero patients
options.B: Excessive supplies of clean water and electricity
options.C: An overwhelming surplus of highly paid medical doctors in every village
options.D: Chronic underfunding and shortages of essential drugs

explanation: Correct. Sadly, many primary health centers struggle with basic funding, poor infrastructure, and running out of essential medicines.

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful reason for a nurse to take a detailed diet and job history from a patient?

options.A: To check for foods that might block or speed up liver enzymes
options.B: To identify workplace toxins that could alter drug breakdown
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of the patient's groceries
options.D: To uncover nutritional shortages that affect blood protein levels

explanation: While finances matter in real life, a patient's grocery budget doesn't directly change how their body processes drugs—unlike their diet, job toxins, and protein intake! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h6)

question: What is the correct step to take the moment a sharps container hits its fill line?

options.A: Leave the lid open for the next shift to use
options.B: Press the contents down firmly with your hand
options.C: Lock the lid securely and prepare for disposal
options.D: Empty the contents into a regular black bin

explanation: Locking the lid right away stops accidental spills and keeps protruding needles from injuring anyone.

question: What is one of the most common signs of caregiver burnout in family members looking after an aging relative?

options.A: Physical exhaustion and emotional strain
options.B: An immediate surplus of personal free time
options.C: Increased desire to learn complex medical procedures
options.D: Improved sleeping patterns and high energy

explanation: Exactly. Looking after a loved one around the clock without breaks is exhausting, often leading to deep physical tiredness and emotional stress.

question: A patient with persistent asthma is prescribed a daily inhaler that works for 12 hours. What drug class is this?

options.A: Short-acting anticholinergics
options.B: Short-Acting Beta-Agonists
options.C: Long-Acting Beta-Agonists
options.D: Inhaled corticosteroids

explanation: That's a Long-Acting Beta-Agonist (LABA)! While SABAs are for quick rescue, LABAs provide steady, long-lasting control throughout the day.

question: When can palliative care be started for someone with a serious illness?

options.A: Only when the patient is discharged back home
options.B: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.C: After all medical treatments have completely failed
options.D: Early in the disease course alongside curative treatments

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the very end! It can start right from diagnosis, walking hand-in-hand with treatments meant to cure or manage the disease.

question: What do we call the solid little ball of cells that forms a few days after fertilization?

options.A: Zygote
options.B: Blastocyst
options.C: Morula
options.D: Trophoblast

explanation: You got it! It's called a morula, looking like a tiny, solid cluster of cells before it hollows out into the next stage.

question: A patient arrives pale, dizzy, and bleeding heavily after an unsafe abortion. What action should you take right away?

options.A: Perform a complete pelvic exam without checking vital signs
options.B: Start a large-bore intravenous line for fluid resuscitation
options.C: Ask the patient to write down a detailed confession of the act
options.D: Wait for the attending physician to arrive before acting

explanation: You got this! When someone is bleeding heavily, getting IV access fast is crucial to restore fluids, boost blood volume, and prevent shock.

question: Your IV patient suddenly feels short of breath, has crackles in their lungs, and high blood pressure. What do you do first?

options.A: Slow the infusion rate, elevate the head of the bed, and notify the provider
options.B: Flush the line rapidly with a bolus of normal saline to check patency
options.C: Place the client flat on their left side and prepare for emergency intubation
options.D: Remove the IV cannula immediately and apply a cold ice pack to the limb

explanation: Classic signs of fluid overload! Slowing the fluids and sitting the patient up helps them breathe easier while you alert the doctor.

question: Which type of abuse involves controlling money and financial resources to keep power over a partner?

options.A: Psychological abuse
options.B: Economic abuse
options.C: Physical abuse
options.D: Sexual abuse

explanation: Economic abuse traps people by cutting them off from money, jobs, and financial freedom. Spotting this helps us understand the full picture of abuse.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing duty under the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: Educating mothers on exclusive breastfeeding practices
options.B: Conducting routine antenatal assessments and checkups
options.C: Administering childhood immunizations according to the schedule
options.D: Performing elective major surgeries in primary health clinics

explanation: Correct! Major surgeries belong in a surgical theater with a doctor, not at a basic primary health clinic.

question: Why is helping clients connect with their community an important part of day and night hospital care?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any ongoing medication
options.B: It reduces stigma and helps clients function within their social environment
options.C: It ensures patients never have to return to their families
options.D: It allows the hospital to discharge staff and save money

explanation: You got it! Keeping clients connected to their communities builds acceptance and supports long-term recovery.

question: Why should nurses involve local community leaders when starting health programs?

options.A: It gives leaders legal authority to write nursing prescriptions
options.B: It replaces the need for trained healthcare professionals
options.C: It builds local support and ensures programs respect cultural values
options.D: It prevents community members from asking questions

explanation: Working with local leaders builds trust and makes sure the community welcomes and accepts the health program.

question: A patient develops a tension pneumothorax after trauma, leading to muffled heart sounds and falling blood pressure. Which type of shock is this?

options.A: Obstructive shock
options.B: Distributive shock
options.C: Cardiogenic shock
options.D: Hypovolemic shock

explanation: When something physical—like trapped air pressing on the heart—blocks normal blood flow through the vessels, we call it obstructive shock. Clear the blockage, and you save the day!

question: What is the primary goal of applying trauma-informed principles immediately after a community disaster?

options.A: To enforce strict behavioral rules and curfews across the neighborhood
options.B: To immediately diagnose every resident with post-traumatic stress disorder
options.C: To gather clinical research data for academic publication
options.D: To build safety, de-escalate fear, and help stabilize the population

explanation: Trauma-informed disaster response prioritizes safety and trust to calm affected individuals and prevent further psychological harm. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which type of patient benefits the most from an advanced smart bed?

options.A: An outpatient arriving for routine diagnostic blood work
options.B: An alert adult patient who walks independently to the bathroom
options.C: A patient with severe mobility impairments and high pressure ulcer risk
options.D: A young child admitted for short-term observation of mild dehydration

explanation: Smart beds are lifesavers for vulnerable patients who can't move themselves and need extra help keeping their skin safe.

question: What is the main goal of disaster mitigation?

options.A: To completely eliminate all natural hazards on earth
options.B: To manage patients only after a disaster has occurred
options.C: To reduce the severity and impact of potential disasters
options.D: To provide immediate funding for post-disaster recovery

explanation: You've got this! Mitigation is all about lessening the damage from hazards that we cannot completely stop.

question: Which of the following is an example of an administrative control?

options.A: Rotating staff away from high-noise areas to limit exposure time
options.B: Replacing a toxic cleaning fluid with warm water and soap
options.C: Providing heavy leather boots to construction workers
options.D: Installing a heavy glass shield around a loud machine

explanation: Changing work schedules and rotating job duties to limit exposure time are classic administrative controls. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h5)

question: What is the actual impact of FGM on childbirth, contrary to traditional beliefs?

options.A: Delivery times become much shorter and completely painless
options.B: The procedure permanently cures all forms of primary infertility
options.C: Scar tissue obstructs labor and increases childbirth risks
options.D: Hormonal levels rise significantly to support healthy pregnancies

explanation: Spot on! Instead of helping, FGM creates tough scar tissue that causes serious complications during delivery.

question: A young female client has extra facial hair, acne, and irregular periods. Which condition matches these signs?

options.A: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.B: Primary amenorrhea
options.C: Endometriosis
options.D: Pelvic organ prolapse

explanation: Great job! PCOS involves high male hormone levels (androgens), leading to signs like unwanted hair growth, acne, and irregular monthly cycles.

question: Which of these is a direct clinical duty for a nurse caring for an FGM survivor?

options.A: Performing corrective cosmetic surgeries in outpatient wards
options.B: Managing chronic pain and obstetric complications
options.C: Isolating the patient from traditional community networks
options.D: Reporting family members immediately to international courts

explanation: Correct! As a nurse, you provide physical and emotional care for the lasting health issues caused by the procedure.

question: What triggers the sudden mood swings and emotional shifts right after childbirth?

options.A: The total exhaustion of red blood cells in the brain
options.B: An abnormal buildup of carbon dioxide in brain tissue
options.C: A sudden increase in thyroid hormone production by the liver
options.D: The rapid drop in placental hormones like estrogen and progesterone

explanation: You've got this! Delivering the placenta causes a sudden drop in hormones, which can temporarily rock the nervous system and cause emotional ups and downs.

question: Why is the intracardiac injection route hardly ever used in modern hospitals anymore?

options.A: Patients refusing to allow needles near their chests
options.B: New laws making emergency heart surgery illegal
options.C: The high cost of manufacturing long needles
options.D: The availability of safer and easier intraosseous and IV routes

explanation: Medical tech has advanced! Today's intraosseous drills and central lines deliver drugs super fast without putting a giant needle directly through the heart.

question: Which nerve from the brachial plexus supplies the triceps muscle and extends the wrist?

options.A: Median nerve
options.B: Musculocutaneous nerve
options.C: Ulnar nerve
options.D: Radial nerve

explanation: The radial nerve runs along the posterior aspect of the upper limb and is responsible for extending the elbow, wrist, and fingers. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical local issue at a subcutaneous injection site?

options.A: Hematoma formation
options.B: Mild local bruising
options.C: Anaphylactic shock
options.D: Sterile abscess

explanation: You've got this! Anaphylaxis is a full-body allergic reaction, not just a local problem happening right at the patch of skin where the injection went in.

question: What is the primary job of the respiratory center in the medulla?

options.A: Filtering dust and germs out of inhaled air
options.B: Setting the basic rhythm and depth of breathing
options.C: Exchanging oxygen across the lung membranes
options.D: Producing mucus to keep the airway moist

explanation: The medullary respiratory center automatically drives the inhale-and-exhale cycle without needing conscious thought. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h4)

question: What is the main goal that drives private companies in the food supply business?

options.A: Providing completely free meals to every global citizen
options.B: Financial profit and commercial return on investment
options.C: Enforcing international public health laws and safety codes
options.D: Eliminating the need for government agricultural policies

explanation: Private agribusinesses and food corporations are businesses, so their main engine is making a profit from what they sell.

question: What does a risk assessment mainly look at?

options.A: The speed at which emergency vehicles can travel
options.B: The exact budget needed to rebuild a damaged clinic
options.C: The likelihood of a hazard and population vulnerability
options.D: The personal medical history of disaster survivors

explanation: Spot on! Risk assessment combines how likely an event is with how exposed and vulnerable the people are.

question: A hospital completely bans the use of a toxic chemical sterilizing agent and buys a safe machine instead. Which control strategy is this?

options.A: Administrative control
options.B: Work practice change
options.C: Elimination
options.D: Personal protection

explanation: Removing the toxic chemical completely from the facility means the hazard has been eliminated. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h3)

question: Which chronic medical condition is a leading cause of peripheral neuropathy?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Essential hypertension
options.C: Diabetes mellitus
options.D: Asthma

explanation: Long-term high blood sugar levels commonly damage peripheral nerves, making diabetes the most frequent cause of neuropathy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h9)

question: What should an instructor do if students keep struggling to understand a concept after a lesson?

options.A: Blame the students for lacking basic intelligence
options.B: Ignore the failure and move on to the next chapter
options.C: Remove all practical work from the nursing curriculum
options.D: Revise the activity or adjust the teaching method

explanation: If a topic is tough to grasp, a good educator changes the approach so everyone can succeed. Learning is a two-way street!

question: How does a nurse's role shift when a patient moves from Tier 3 up to Tier 4?

options.A: The nurse stops assessing mental health and focuses only on surgery
options.B: The nurse focuses only on providing food and shelter
options.C: The nurse shifts from general supportive counseling to specialized psychiatric nursing care like medication management
options.D: The nurse stops caring for the patient entirely

explanation: As needs become more complex at the top of the pyramid, nursing care shifts toward specialized psychiatric support, such as managing prescribed medications.

question: A nurse records a patient's daily urine output as 1000 mL, which is exactly double yesterday's output. What scale makes this math possible?

options.A: Ratio scale
options.B: Interval scale
options.C: Ordinal scale
options.D: Nominal scale

explanation: Because urine output has a true zero (0 mL means absolutely no urine), you can safely make direct comparisons like 'twice as much'.

question: A community health nurse wants to understand why mothers refuse to bring babies for routine immunization. Which data collection method is best suited for this?

options.A: Measuring the height and weight of newborn babies
options.B: Checking the expiration dates of vaccines in the clinic fridge
options.C: Counting the number of cars passing through the main highway
options.D: Focus group discussions with local nursing mothers

explanation: Focus group discussions allow mothers to openly share their personal beliefs, fears, and cultural concerns regarding immunization. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the first step evaluated during the primary survey of an emergency patient?

options.A: Circulation
options.B: Breathing
options.C: Airway
options.D: Disability

explanation: The primary survey strictly follows the ABCDE mnemonic, placing airway assessment and management at the very top. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h4)

question: A community experiences a sudden outbreak of severe diarrhea linked to contaminated street food. What is the most appropriate regulatory response?

options.A: Blame consumers for choosing to eat outside their homes
options.B: Wait for the outbreak to resolve itself without investigating the source
options.C: Inspect food handling practices and provide hygiene education to vendors
options.D: Ban the sale of all food items in the entire country permanently

explanation: Targeted inspections and education address the root cause of contamination while supporting safe local commerce. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h4)

question: What does 'statistical power' mean in a research study?

options.A: The physical strength required by nurses to lift heavy patients
options.B: The total amount of funding secured for laboratory equipment
options.C: The ability of the study to detect a true effect if one exists
options.D: The speed at which data is entered into a computer spreadsheet

explanation: You got it! Power is basically your study's muscle—its ability to catch a real treatment difference if it's actually there.

question: Why does the formal healthcare system train Traditional Birth Attendants (TBAs)?

options.A: Licensing them to perform major surgical operations independently
options.B: Replacing all professional midwives in urban hospitals
options.C: Employing them as permanent government administrative officers
options.D: Teaching them to recognize danger signs and refer complicated labor early

explanation: Exactly right! Since many mothers still visit TBAs, training them to spot danger signs early helps save lives by getting women to the hospital fast when trouble arises.

question: Why is serious damage to the medulla oblongata so dangerous?

options.A: It coordinates voluntary muscle movement for walking
options.B: It stores long-term memory and learning skills
options.C: It produces cerebrospinal fluid for the brain
options.D: It controls basic functions that keep us alive

explanation: Because it houses vital control centers for breathing and heart rate, injury here quickly stops life-sustaining processes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h1)

question: Who is the expert behind the System of Profound Knowledge framework?

options.A: Jean Watson
options.B: W. Edwards Deming
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Abraham Maslow

explanation: W. Edwards Deming created this framework to help workplaces improve continuously and make quality care easier for everyone.

question: What is the main goal of the controlling function in nursing management?

options.A: Recruiting qualified nursing personnel for open shifts
options.B: Punishing staff members who make clinical documentation errors
options.C: Monitoring activities to ensure they meet established goals
options.D: Creating brand new institutional policies from scratch

explanation: Think of controlling as checking in to make sure your ward's care and daily targets match what the hospital planned to achieve. You're doing great!

question: A client on a strict budget needs affordable protein. Which of these is the best recommendation?

options.A: Packaged beef jerky
options.B: Beans and local eggs
options.C: Imported salmon fillets
options.D: Processed protein powders

explanation: You got it! Beans and local eggs are cheap, easy to find, and give fantastic protein without burning a hole in your pocket.

question: Why must you use the same data collection tools throughout a longitudinal study?

options.A: To make sure the research assistants do not have to work very hard
options.B: To ensure that measured changes are real and not caused by changing the measurement tool
options.C: To comply with rules about destroying old medical records
options.D: To keep the total budget of the research project at zero

explanation: Exactly! If you change your measuring instrument, you won't know if patient scores changed because their health changed or simply because the tool was different.

question: How can a severe head injury lead to epilepsy months or years down the line?

options.A: Brain scarring creates an irritable focus for abnormal electrical discharges
options.B: Initial trauma destroys the pituitary gland completely
options.C: Chronic blood loss depletes the brain of necessary oxygen
options.D: Skull fractures permanently alter intracranial pressure gradients

explanation: When brain tissue heals from trauma, it can form scar tissue. This scar can irritate nearby neurons and trigger abnormal electrical bursts later on.

question: Why is asking about family and home life so important when assessing a patient with a skin rash?

options.A: It replaces the need for a physical skin examination
options.B: It helps identify if other household members share the same contact infection
options.C: It determines the exact antibiotic resistance profile of the organism
options.D: It proves whether the patient has a genetic predisposition to eczema

explanation: Contact infections love to bounce around families! Checking if others at home are scratching stops the vicious cycle of reinfection.

question: Why are elderly patients especially prone to severe confusion during emergency evacuations?

options.A: They frequently lose essential sensory aids like glasses and hearing aids
options.B: They are naturally immune to psychological shock and trauma
options.C: They prefer to ignore instructions given by emergency staff
options.D: Their medical conditions prevent them from feeling fear

explanation: You nailed it! Losing glasses or hearing aids in a sudden rush cuts older adults off from their surroundings, making confusion and anxiety spike.

question: Why is losing a pulse considered a very late and dangerous sign of compartment syndrome?

options.A: Arteries have thick walls and are the last vessels to collapse under pressure.
options.B: Pulse checks are unreliable unless done with a special electronic machine.
options.C: Blood flow actually increases in the early stages of compartment pressure.
options.D: Nerves stop working before blood vessels even begin to narrow.

explanation: Major arteries are tough and hold out the longest. Nerves and tiny capillaries get crushed and starved of oxygen way before the main pulse disappears.

question: Which communication tool remains especially reliable for reaching remote areas during electrical power failures?

options.A: Automated email newsletters
options.B: Battery-powered radios
options.C: Personal office computers
options.D: High-speed fiber internet

explanation: Radios that run on batteries do not rely on local power grids or internet access, making them resilient during blackouts. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why should you never point a used sharp device toward your own body?

options.A: It causes the medication inside to evaporate quickly
options.B: It makes the needle dull for future patients
options.C: It increases the chance of a direct puncture injury
options.D: It violates hospital rules regarding uniform neatness

explanation: Keep sharp points facing away from you so that if your hand slips, you won't get poked.
